profile.name: Jos Buttler
profile.writeup:
Defined by explosive wrist speed, uninhibited creativity, and devastating power down the order, Jos Buttler established himself as one of the most transformative white-ball batters of his generation. Emerging from Somerset, the right-handed wicketkeeper-batter revolutionized English limited-overs batting through an expansive repertoire that blends orthodox hitting with audacious ramp shots, scoops, and power-clearing down the ground. Possessing incredible hand-eye coordination, Buttler redefined the role of middle-order finisher before seamlessly evolving into a dominant white-ball opener.


Buttler brings a calm, calculated intensity to the middle, pairing a cool demeanour under pressure with an explosive scoring rate. Behind the stumps, his clean athleticism and swift reactions made him a mainstay for England across formats, while his tactical clarity naturally elevated him to team leadership. As England's white-ball captain following Eoin Morgan's retirement, Buttler cemented his legacy by leading England to glory at the 2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup in Australia, making England the first men's team to hold both the 50-over and 20-over World Cup titles simultaneously.


His white-ball career is littered with iconic match-winning displays. During England's historic 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup campaign on home soil, Buttler played a vital role, scoring 59 in the final at Lord's and subsequently executing the decisive run-out in the Super Over to seal England's first 50-over World Cup trophy. In T20 Internationals, he scored a brilliant maiden century against Sri Lanka during the 2021 T20 World Cup, proving his ability to anchor an innings on tough subcontinental surfaces before unleashing late-over destruction.


In global domestic leagues, Buttler became a marquee international superstar, most notably in the Indian Premier League (IPL) representing the Rajasthan Royals. His finest IPL campaign arrived in 2022, where he delivered one of the most dominant individual seasons in league history, smashing four centuries and compiling 863 runs to claim the Most Valuable Player award and the Orange Cap. In Test cricket, though used periodically, Buttler demonstrated remarkable adaptability, highlighted by a counter-attacking maiden Test century against India at Trent Bridge in 2018.


His individual brilliance has been validated by top honours within English and international cricket. He was named in the ICC T20I Team of the Year in 2021, recognized as the Young Wisden Schools Cricketer of the Year in 2010, and appointed an MBE in the 2020 New Year Honours list for services to cricket. A modern pioneer, Buttler stands as an architect of England's white-ball revolution whose match-winning flair continues to shape short-format cricket.
